title: Gorenstein Duality of the Two-Generator Semigroup Ring (Hypersurface Presentation)

problemStatement.formal: S = \langle a,b\rangle \text{ symmetric} \implies k[t^a, t^b] \text{ is Gorenstein}
problemStatement.plain: The parent open question asks to bridge the combinatorial symmetry of the two-generator numerical semigroup $\langle a,b\rangle$ (already formalized in frobenius-number-oq-01-oq-03: $PF(\langle a,b\rangle)=\{g\}$, type one — the Gorenstein/symmetric condition) to commutative algebra: that the semigroup ring $k[t^a,t^b]$ is Gorenstein. The honest tractable realization is the hypersurface presentation $k[X_0,X_1]/(X_0^b - X_1^a) \cong k[t^a,t^b]$ exhibiting the ring as a complete intersection (hence Gorenstein).

knowledge.markdown:
# Knowledge Base: frobenius-number-oq-02-oq-02

## Problem

Bridge the combinatorial symmetry of ⟨a,b⟩ to the commutative-algebra statement that k[t^a,t^b] is Gorenstein.

## Session 2026-07-01 (Session 1, FRESH → SURVEY/ORIENT)

### Findings

- **Combinatorial core already done.** `frobenius-number-oq-01-oq-03` proves ⟨a,b⟩ has type one / PF(⟨a,b⟩)={g}; its own docstring names this 'the Gorenstein/symmetric condition'. Nothing left to do combinatorially.
- **Mathlib gap (verified by grep).** No Gorenstein, Cohen–Macaulay, or canonical/dualizing-module theory exists in the pinned Mathlib. The literal ring-theoretic Gorenstein statement is BLOCKED (>1000 lines of foundational commutative algebra to build).
- **Tractable bridge = hypersurface presentation.** k[X0,X1]/(X0^b−X1^a) ≅ k[t^a,t^b]. A one-relation quotient (hypersurface) is automatically Gorenstein, so this is the concrete, expressible content.

### Scaffold (UNVERIFIED — build-blocked by full disk)

`proofs/Proofs/FrobeniusNumberOQ02OQ02.lean`:
- `phi` : presentation map k[X0,X1] → k[t], X0↦t^a, X1↦t^b.
- `range_phi` : range φ = Algebra.adjoin K {t^a, t^b} (image = semigroup ring).
- `relation_mem_ker` : φ(X0^b − X1^a) = 0.
- `span_le_ker` : (X0^b − X1^a) ⊆ ker φ (presentation surjection).

The hard reverse inclusion ker φ ⊆ (X0^b − X1^a) (the complete-intersection isomorphism) is the follow-up.

### Build/tooling blockers this session

- Host disk 100% full (~2Gi free, falling); `lake env lean` on the scaffold hit torn-olean `invalid header` then segfault (RC=139) — infra, not the code.
- Aristotle MCP returned `Resource not found` (service unavailable).

### Next

1. Verify scaffold on a healthy disk (expected clean) → ship as verified 0-axiom gallery entry.
2. Prove the kernel equality (monomial-curve complete intersection) via reduction argument or Aristotle.
